# atlas reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask skill` from the code; do not edit. A test fails when it drifts. -->

Everything atlas takes, generated from the code the server answers from. The habits and the workflow are in `SKILL.md`. The tools section is the help text the server sends as `atlas://help` (also `note op=help`).

## Queue commands

- `atlas queue list [--lane LANE]`
- `atlas queue show KEY`
- `atlas queue drop KEY`
- `atlas queue done KEY`
- `atlas queue met KEY [CONDITION]`
- `atlas queue next [--transcript PATH]`
- `atlas queue release SLOT|AGENT|LANE [--force]`
- `atlas queue release AGENT --transcript PATH [--force]`
- `atlas queue add --description TEXT [--kind KIND] FILE|-`
- `atlas queue plan --lane LANE --title TEXT [--kind KIND] [--priority P] [--uses LIST] [--after LIST] [--order N] [--scope TEXT] [--ticket KEY]`
- `atlas queue plan --from-jql QUERY [--kind KIND] [--priority P] [--uses LIST] [--after LIST] [--scope TEXT] [--order-from N] [--lane-from key|fixed:LANE] [--limit N]`

## atlas tools

Answers are plain text; `format: "json"` gives JSON. A repeated read answers `unchanged since ... #N`, or only the lines that changed: per agent with the hooks on, per server without them (the earlier call may be another agent's); `fresh: true` gives the whole answer. `read_note` takes `lines` (`A-B`) or `budget_tokens`, on a vault or a source. Each op runs the full tool named after it, and every argument of that tool is accepted (the listed schemas name the common ones). The full tool names also work as tool names, for one release.

### Listed tools

- `lookup`: Where an identifier is defined and mentioned; without id, list identifiers.
  - without `id` runs `ids`
- `search`: Lines in vaults, or ranked sections of every vault and source (sections, semantic, hybrid).
- `section`: One section's exact text by heading or id, with file and lines.
- `grep`: Regex over the indexed vaults and sources, with context lines.
- `symbol`: Code symbol: definitions, references with their caller, impls.
- `recall`: Memory by key (or h:ID), query or lane; op status: lanes, op log: versions.
  - op `status` runs `journal_status`
  - op `log` runs `memory_log`
  - op `sweep` runs `question_sweep`
  - op `deferred` runs `deferred_questions`
  - `key` `h:ID` (a digest's handle) reads that stored output: its first page, or one of `lines` (A-B), `item`, `failures`, `grep` (with `context`), `head`, `tail`, `page`, `digest`; a hint line `recall h:ID lines=A-B` is those arguments, and they may also follow the id in `key`; `key` `h:` lists the newest
- `remember`: Store a memory, rule or decision; revising needs expected_sha; old: supersede.
  - with `old` runs `supersede`
- `journal`: Append a lane journal entry: lane, entry, text. Review meta: role:, pr:, head:, verdict:.
  - entry `queued` files planned work, as `atlas queue plan` does: the text's first line is the title, the rest its scope; `meta` lines `kind:`, `priority:`, `uses:`, `after:` (queue keys or free text) and `order:` are checked, other lines kept
  - entry `review` files a review for the merge gate (`orchestrate.reviews`): `meta` lines `role:`, `pr:`, `head:` (the sha read), `verdict:` (pass, merge, merge with follow-ups, request changes) and `report:`
  - `amend: KEY` with `expected_sha` (the head's sha) rewrites that entry's title and body as a new version; its lane, entry, meta lines and refs stay (pass the same `lane` and `entry`, no `meta` or `refs`)
- `handoff`: Write a lane handoff (allowed past the context cap).
- `note`: Vault notes, read only. op read: the whole note; section is cheaper for one heading. op help: every op and argument.
  - op `read` runs `read_note`
  - op `list` runs `list_notes`
  - op `find` runs `find_by_frontmatter`
  - op `backlinks` runs `backlinks`
  - op `outlinks` runs `outlinks`
  - op `broken` runs `broken_links`
  - op `link` runs `make_link`
  - op `log` runs `write_log`
  - op `vaults` runs `list_vaults`
  - op `sources` runs `list_sources`
  - op `judge` runs `judge_task`
- `edit`: Write vault notes; never deletes.
  - op `create` runs `create_note`
  - op `append` runs `append_to_note`
  - op `history` runs `append_history`
  - op `frontmatter` runs `set_frontmatter`
  - op `section` runs `replace_section`
  - op `link` runs `link_notes`
  - op `next_id` runs `next_id`
  - op `index` runs `build_index`
  - op `refresh` runs `refresh_index`
  - op `refresh_all` runs `refresh_all_indices`
  - op `link`: `vault` and `path` are the note the link is written into
- `discuss`: Discussion threads and the decision queue. conclude, unresolved, decide: see note op=help.
  - op `open` runs `open_discussion`
  - op `post` runs `post`
  - op `read` runs `read_discussion`
  - op `status` runs `discussion_status`
  - op `awaiting` runs `awaiting`
  - op `list` runs `list_discussions`
  - op `queue` runs `decision_queue`
  - op `conclude` runs `conclude_discussion`
  - op `unresolved` runs `mark_unresolved`
  - op `decide` runs `record_decision`
- `miss`: Misses: report what atlas did not return, list them, resolve one.
  - op `report` runs `report_miss`
  - op `list` runs `misses`
  - op `resolve` runs `resolve_miss`
- `hook`: Claude Code hook entry point; not for models.

### Full tools

#### list_vaults

Served vaults and note counts.


#### list_notes

Notes in a vault folder: path, title, size, sha256.

- `vault` string, required
- `folder` string
- `glob` string: * ? **; no '/' matches the file name.
- `recursive` boolean: Default true.
- `limit` integer: Default 500.

#### read_note

A note's whole text and sha256; lines or budget_tokens for part of it. For one heading, section is the cheaper read.

- `vault` string, required
- `path` string, required
- `lines` string: A-B, A- or A: only these lines (from 1).
- `budget_tokens` integer: Whole lines up to about this many tokens; a +N more lines line names the rest.

#### search

Search lines (substring, regex, fts) in vaults, or rank sections of every vault and source (sections; semantic and hybrid by meaning).

- `query` string, required: sections: words, "quoted phrase".
- `mode` string (substring, regex, fts, sections, semantic, hybrid)
- `vault` string
- `source` string: sections: one source or vault.
- `folder` string
- `case_sensitive` boolean
- `raw` boolean: sections: query is FTS5 syntax.
- `full` boolean: sections: whole section text, not snippets.
- `refresh` string (auto, check, off): Stale files: auto reindexes a few (default), check reports.
- `limit` integer: Default 50; sections 5.
- `format` string (text, json)
- `verbose` boolean: Add scan times and timings.

#### lookup

Where an identifier is defined and mentioned, across every vault and source.

- `id` string, required
- `limit` integer: Mention lines, default 3.
- `full` boolean: Every definition's whole text.
- `refresh` string (auto, check, off): Stale files: auto reindexes a few (default), check reports.
- `format` string (text, json)
- `verbose` boolean: Add scan times and timings.

#### symbol

Code symbol (Rust, WGSL, Protobuf, Go, TS/JS, C#, Python, Java; Kotlin and other files definitions only): definitions, references with their caller, impls.

- `name` string, required: Name or Type::name.
- `limit` integer: References, default 10.
- `format` string (text, json)
- `verbose` boolean: Add scan times and timings.

#### ids

Registered identifiers: kind, definitions, occurrences, newest date.

- `prefix` string
- `pattern` string: Regex.
- `kind` string
- `source` string
- `limit` integer: Default 50.
- `refresh` string (auto, check, off): Stale files: auto reindexes a few (default), check reports.
- `format` string (text, json)
- `verbose` boolean: Add scan times and timings.

#### list_sources

Vaults and sources: root, files, sections.

- `format` string (text, json)
- `verbose` boolean: Add scan times and timings.

#### judge_task

The task judge's model and effort pick for an agent launch prompt, as a Judge line to paste (orchestrate.judge.cells).

- `prompt` string, required: The launch prompt.
- `kind` string (reviewer, builder, research, other)
- `subagent_type` string
- `description` string: The launch's description.

#### report_miss

Record something grep or reading found that atlas did not return. (writes)

- `tool` string (lookup, ids, search, list_sources, other), required
- `query` string, required
- `returned` string
- `found` string, required: path:line or description.
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### misses

Recorded misses, newest first.

- `status` string (open, resolved, all)
- `limit` integer: Default 20.
- `format` string (text, json)
- `verbose` boolean: Add scan times and timings.

#### resolve_miss

Mark a miss resolved. (writes)

- `id` integer, required
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### find_by_frontmatter

Notes whose frontmatter key equals a value (any list item; case-insensitive), or has the key.

- `key` string, required
- `value` string
- `prefix` boolean: Value starts with `value`.
- `vault` string
- `folder` string
- `limit` integer: Default 500.

#### backlinks

Links into a note from every vault.

- `vault` string, required
- `path` string, required

#### outlinks

Links in a note, resolved (null when missing).

- `vault` string, required
- `path` string, required

#### broken_links

Links whose target note does not exist.

- `vault` string

#### write_log

The audit log of writes, newest first.

- `vault` string
- `path` string
- `client` string
- `since` string: UTC, inclusive.
- `until` string: UTC, exclusive.
- `discussion` string
- `limit` integer: Default 100.

#### make_link

Link text to a note: [[wikilink]] in one vault, obsidian:// across vaults.

- `from_vault` string, required
- `to_vault` string, required
- `path` string, required
- `heading` string
- `text` string

#### link_notes

Append a link to the target under a section of the source note, once. (writes)

- `from_vault` string, required
- `from_path` string, required
- `to_vault` string, required
- `to_path` string, required
- `heading` string
- `section` string: Default Related.
- `reverse` boolean: Link back too.
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### create_note

Create a note; fails if it exists. (writes)

- `vault` string, required
- `path` string, required
- `content` string, required
- `create_folders` boolean
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### append_to_note

Append text to a note. (writes)

- `vault` string, required
- `path` string, required
- `text` string, required
- `expected_sha256` string: Refuse unless the note's sha256 matches.
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### append_history

Append '- YYYY-MM-DD: text' under '## History'. (writes)

- `vault` string, required
- `path` string, required
- `text` string, required
- `date` string: Default today.
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### set_frontmatter

Set frontmatter keys; the rest stays byte-identical. (writes)

- `vault` string, required
- `path` string, required
- `values` object, required
- `expected_sha256` string: Refuse unless the note's sha256 matches.
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### replace_section

Replace the body under a heading, or the preamble (heading ""). (writes)

- `vault` string, required
- `path` string, required
- `heading` string: Without # marks.
- `preamble` boolean
- `level` integer
- `content` string, required
- `expected_sha256` string, required
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### next_id

Allocate the next id of a sequence (PI-244); with name and content, create '<folder>/<id> <name>.md' ({{id}} replaced). (writes)

- `vault` string, required
- `folder` string, required
- `prefix` string, required: e.g. PI-.
- `digits` integer: Default 3.
- `name` string
- `content` string
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### build_index

Write a generated index of notes between markers in a note (see README for spec). (writes)

- `vault` string, required
- `path` string, required
- `name` string, required
- `spec` object, required
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### refresh_index

Regenerate the indices in one note. (writes)

- `vault` string, required
- `path` string, required
- `name` string
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### refresh_all_indices

Regenerate every index. (writes)

- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### open_discussion

Open a thread Discussions/D-### <topic>.md with P-1. (writes)

- `vault` string, required
- `topic` string, required
- `subjects` array, required
- `participants` array, required
- `opening_post` object, required

#### post

Append a post to a thread. Correct with a retract; kinds other than claim and question need re. (writes)

- `thread` string, required: vault:D-004 or vault:path.
- `author` string, required
- `kind` string (claim, evidence, challenge, answer, concede, retract, question, proposal), required
- `body` string, required
- `re` integer: P-number replied to.

#### read_discussion

A thread's posts, integrity check and outcomes.

- `thread` string, required: vault:D-004 or vault:path.
- `since_post` integer

#### discussion_status

Each claim, challenge and question's state in a thread.

- `thread` string, required: vault:D-004 or vault:path.

#### awaiting

Challenges and questions to an author still unanswered.

- `author` string, required
- `vault` string

#### conclude_discussion

Append a verdict and conclude; refused while contested unless force_reason. (writes)

- `thread` string, required: vault:D-004 or vault:path.
- `verdict_body` string, required
- `author` string
- `force_reason` string
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.

#### mark_unresolved

End a thread without agreement, for a human decision. (writes)

- `thread` string, required: vault:D-004 or vault:path.
- `summary` string, required
- `open_questions` array, required
- `positions` array, required
- `settle_by` string, required
- `author` string
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.

#### record_decision

Settle an unresolved thread with a decision post. (writes)

- `thread` string, required: vault:D-004 or vault:path.
- `decided_by` string, required
- `decision` string, required
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.

#### list_discussions

Threads with status, participants and counts.

- `vault` string
- `status` string (open, concluded, parked, unresolved)
- `subject` string
- `needs_decision` boolean

#### decision_queue

Unresolved threads, oldest first.

- `repo` string: Only threads naming this repo of the active project or a repo it talks to or is used by.

#### remember

Store a memory, rule or decision (new key: create; existing key: new version, needs expected_sha). Never deletes. (writes)

- `kind` string (memory, rule, decision), required
- `key` string: Memory slug; rules and decisions get one.
- `title` string: One line; a memory's or a rule's is at most 120 characters.
- `summary` string: Memory: index description, one line of at most 200 characters.
- `body` string, required
- `sub` string: Memory type (user, feedback, project, reference).
- `scope` string: user: the shared user layer, seen in every project (memories only).
- `refs` array: kind:target, e.g. lane:x, commit:abc.
- `expected_sha` string: Head sha (or its first 12+ hex digits), to revise.
- `export` string: Export to place it in.
- `after` string: Place right after this key.
- `author` string: Who asked.
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.

#### recall

Memory records by key (history: true for versions), by query (best whole, the rest as pointers), or a lane's journal (lane). Key h:ID reads a stored output (a digest's handle): its first page, or one selector; key h: lists the newest.

- `key` string: A record key, or h:ID (a stored output), or h: (list them).
- `query` string
- `lane` string
- `kind` string
- `scope` string
- `history` boolean
- `limit` integer: Default 8 (20 for h:).
- `budget_tokens` integer
- `lines` string: h:ID only: lines A-B.
- `item` string: h:ID only: one item by name (a test, error:2, a file, Type::fn).
- `failures` boolean: h:ID only: every failure block.
- `grep` string: h:ID only: lines matching this regex.
- `context` integer: h:ID only, with grep: context lines (default 2).
- `head` integer: h:ID only: the first N lines.
- `tail` integer: h:ID only: the last N lines.
- `page` integer: h:ID only: from line K (a PR file's next page).
- `digest` boolean: h:ID only: the digest again.
- `digest-grep` string: h:ID only: digest rows matching this regex (every issue or hit of a tracker search).

#### supersede

Replace records with a new one; the old stay, marked superseded. The way to record a reversal. (writes)

- `old` array, required: Keys superseded.
- `kind` string (memory, rule, decision)
- `key` string
- `title` string
- `summary` string
- `body` string, required
- `sub` string
- `scope` string
- `refs` array: 
- `author` string
- `reason` string, required: Why (12+ characters, not a placeholder); logged.

#### journal

Append a lane journal entry: brief, decision, measurement (with conditions), commit, question, answered, next, note. amend KEY with expected_sha rewrites one's text. (writes)

- `lane` string, required
- `entry` string (brief, decision, measurement, commit, question, answered, next, note, cap, checkpoint, queued, review, idea, defer, reopen), required
- `text` string, required: First line is the headline.
- `meta` string: key: value lines (branch, worktree, conditions).
- `refs` array: answers:<key> for an answered question (a decision or answered entry gets it itself for an open question of its lane whose Q-id leads one of its lines, or that it names as answers <key>); reopens:<key> with entry reopen undoes a wrong close; defers:<key> with entry defer, meta until: <UTC time>|next-session and optional proceeding_with: <option>.
- `amend` string: A journal key: rewrite its title and body as a new version (meta and refs kept).
- `expected_sha` string: With amend: the head's sha (recall shows it).

#### handoff

Write a lane handoff (allowed past the context cap). A fresh agent starts from recall lane=<id>. (writes)

- `lane` string, required
- `title` string: One line; default the text's first line.
- `text` string, required
- `refs` array: prior:<key>, commit:<hash>, rule:<key>.

#### journal_status

Active lanes (an open question, a queued entry or a record in the last 14 days): entries, last entry, last commit, open questions, handoffs; then +N idle lanes. all lists every lane.

- `repo` string: Only lanes naming this repo of the active project or a repo it talks to or is used by.
- `all` boolean: Every lane, idle ones too. Default false.

#### memory_log

Memory versions, newest first.

- `key` string
- `kind` string
- `scope` string
- `since` string: UTC time prefix.
- `author` string
- `limit` integer: Default 20.

#### question_sweep

Open questions that look settled, each with its evidence keys (a later decision, answered entry or ruling naming its key or Q-id or sharing its key terms; a merged PR in the lane after it; the lane idle past the stale age). Closes nothing: it prints the one journal entry=answered call with an answers ref per candidate.


#### deferred_questions

Deferred questions (journal entry=defer): the due ones first, each with its options and proceeding_with, to ask as multiple choice; then those still waiting, with their until.


#### hook

Hook entry point for Claude Code mcp_tool hooks; not for models. (writes)

- `event` string, required
- `session_id` string
- `agent_id` string
- `agent_type` string
- `transcript_path` string
- `prompt` string
- `tool_name` string
- `tool_use_id` string
- `tool_prompt` string
- `trigger` string
- `source` string
- `cwd` string
- `permission_mode` string
- `tool_input` string: JSON text.
- `tool_response` string: JSON text.
- `last_assistant_message` string
- `stop_hook_active` string: true or false.
- `background_tasks` string: JSON text.
- `session_crons` string: JSON text.
- `discussion` string: Thread this comes from (vault:D-004).

#### section

One section's exact text by heading or by the id it defines, with its file and line range. Replaces grep -n then sed -n.

- `heading` string: The heading text (case-insensitive), or the end of its heading path (`Parent > Child`).
- `id` string: An identifier: the section that defines it.
- `source` string: Only this vault or source.
- `path` string: Only this file (path below the root).

#### grep

Regex search over the indexed vaults and sources, with context lines. A large result comes back as a digest plus a handle (recall key=h:ID).

- `pattern` string, required: A regular expression, matched per line.
- `source` string: Only this vault or source.
- `path` string: Only paths starting with this (a file or a folder below the root).
- `context` integer: Lines of context around each match (0 to 10, default 0).
